findings.text: package.json bumps version 0.1.4 -> 0.1.5, which the t-1 description does not mention. It fits the release_pipeline/device_uat decisions (tag MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH must equal package.json; v0.1.5 tags), but it is an unplanned change in this task.

yamlSubList (scripts/build-desktop.spec.ts) keeps column-0 '#' comment lines inside the block when computing the minimum indent. One such comment under supportedArchitectures makes the indent 0, so the sub-keys are never matched and the test fails falsely on a valid config.
The darwin libsql test checks more than resolution: it also asserts index.node exists next to each @libsql/darwin-* manifest, which is stronger than the test_contract requires.

scripts/package-desktop.ts fileSize (catch at ~line 1078 of the diff) turns every statSync error into null with no comment, so EACCES or EIO on the APPLE_API_KEY path shows up as 'must name an existing, non-empty .p8 file'. It fails closed and the refusal is printed, but the real error is lost.

The files/asarUnpack tests (matchesAll, packed, unpacked in scripts/package-desktop.spec.ts) check against a hand-copied model of app-builder-lib's filter.js and fileMatcher.js, not electron-builder itself. If electron-builder 26 changes how it collects node_modules, these tests can keep passing while the real packaging changes.

If NSIS gets a null arch for a single-arch build, electron-builder drops '-${arch}' from ARTIFACT_NAME and the installer is named price-check-<v>-win.exe, not ...-win-x64.exe. The spec's expand() always fills in x64, so it can't catch this. Check the real file name before c-4's release job lists its files.
The description says the executor saw 'pnpm package:desktop --version 0.1.4' produce dist-packaged/mac-universal/Price Check.app. That's a manual check the diff can't show.
The tests for refusing --sign also capture process.stdout/stderr and console output, so a leaked secret value would be caught on those paths as well as through the injected stdout/stderr.

scripts/release-tag.spec.ts 'imports only Node built-ins' uses /^import .* from '([^']+)';$/gm. It does not match a multi-line import `import {\n a\n} from 'pkg';` or a side-effect import `import 'pkg';`, so a dependency imported in either form would pass the guard. Matching every `from '...'` / `import '...'` specifier across lines would close the gap.

The test_contract line saying the executor saw `gh api .../environments/release/deployment-branch-policies` return exactly one {name:'v*', type:'tag'} is an executor observation. It is recorded in the task log, not the diff, so this review cannot confirm it.

release.json carries a 'policies' key that the environments PUT endpoint does not accept. The jq projection in the environments.spec.ts header comment strips it before the PUT and sends it through the separate deployment-branch-policies POST, so this is consistent.

The trailing-newline refusal relies on JS `$` without the m flag matching only at end of input. The TAG regex in scripts/release-tag.ts is not multiline, so 'v0.1.5\n' is correctly refused, and the refusal table pins this.

updater-channel.spec's FeedUpdater calls setFeedURL to point the real GitHubProvider at the local fake; this is test-only and the ?raw source guard covers shipped updater.ts, so decision update_flow holds
the 'error' listener is attached in start() before the first runCheck(), and a test checks listenerCount('error') from inside checkForUpdates

src/desktop/lifecycle.ts lockAfterPredecessor: when predecessorPid is set but isProcessAlive is not wired, it returns false with nothing logged, so an update-started launch quits as 'second-instance' without trace. A console.error for that misconfiguration would make it visible.

src/desktop/lifecycle.ts waitForExit: the last probe is at 29750 ms, then it sleeps to 30000 ms and gives up without probing again, logging 'outlived' even if the predecessor exited in that last interval. Harmless, because the lock retry that follows decides, but the log can be wrong.
installPending removes ALERTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY and DATABASE_URL before calling installOnExit, so a failed hand-over still exits with them scrubbed. That is fine because app.exit(0) follows right after.

README tells users the release's .zip and .yml files are for updates, but electron-builder releases usually also carry .blockmap files, which go unmentioned. Harmless, but readers may wonder about them.
The Windows test checks 'SmartScreen' and 'no administrator rights' but not that SmartScreen is the only warning. That is enough for the test_contract, and the 'no UAC' half is device UAT anyway.
The Development section still says 'Electron packaging is in progress', which is a little stale now that releases ship. It is outside this task's claimed surface.

scripts/workflow-reader.ts triggers(): eventAt = body.findIndex(l => pair(l)?.[0] === event) does not check indent, so a nested key (e.g. a workflow_dispatch input named 'push') that comes before the real event line would be taken as that event's body. It should match only at the event's indent (indentOf(body[0])).
stripComment (/\s#.*/) cuts a quoted value that contains ' #' (e.g. key: 'a #b'). The old ci-desktop helpers did the same; this repo's workflows have no such values.
map() now accepts 'KEY:value' with no space after the colon (pinned by the 'H:v' case), unlike the old helper. It is harmless for ci-desktop.spec's env reads.
ci-desktop.spec now reads the workflow in beforeEach. No describe-level code reads the reassigned variables at collection time, so moving the cacheDir/cacheSteps setup is safe.
